name: Lump-Sum Taxation Residence (Forfait Fiscal / Pauschalbesteuerung)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires being a foreign national establishing Swiss residence for the first time (or returning after 10+ years' absence), with no gainful activity in Switzerland — not available to Swiss nationals or anyone who has worked in Switzerland.

This requires a federal minimum taxable base of CHF 435,000 (2026) — the actual base is the HIGHEST of the statutory minimum, 7x annual rent/rental value (for own-household taxpayers, 3x board-and-lodging otherwise), or a control-calculation of Swiss-source income. Cantonal minimums can exceed this federal floor.
requirements.fix_path: Negotiate the taxable base with the relevant cantonal tax authority.

requirements.blocker_text: This is only available in 21 of Switzerland's 26 cantons — Zürich, Schaffhausen, Appenzell Ausserrhoden, Basel-Landschaft, and Basel-Stadt have abolished the regime entirely.

evidence_required.document: Negotiated tax ruling with the cantonal tax authority confirming the taxable base

sources.title: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) — lump-sum taxation, Art. 14 DBG

notes: FORMULA VALUE, THE HIGHEST-RISK STALE FIGURE IN THIS ENTIRE COUNTRY'S DATASET: CHF 435,000 for 2026, up from CHF 434,700 in 2025 — a small but consequential year-over-year change (set by an annual CPI-indexed cold-progression ordinance, AS 2025 579). Multiple secondary sites republish the OLD 2025 figure (CHF 434,700) as current, and others cite entirely fabricated-looking figures (CHF 421,700, CHF 429,700, CHF 451,200) that don't match any confirmed official value for any recent year — this is the single clearest, highest-confidence stale-figure catch found across the Switzerland research pass. GENUINE STRUCTURAL COMPLEXITY: the actual taxable base isn't simply the statutory minimum — it's the HIGHEST of three calculations (statutory floor, 7x rent/rental value, or a control-calculation of Swiss-source income), meaning the real number paid is frequently well above CHF 435,000 for anyone with a substantial Swiss residence. Five cantons (Zürich, Schaffhausen, Appenzell Ausserrhoden, Basel-Landschaft, Basel-Stadt) have ABOLISHED this regime entirely — a real geographic exclusion modeled as a hard requirement here. Uptake data confirmed at tier-1 level is dated: 4,557 persons paid CHF 821 million in tax as of end-2018, the most recent consolidated federal figure identified during research — current-year uptake requires querying individual cantons directly. work_rights is 'none' — genuinely and deliberately excludes gainful activity in Switzerland, the defining feature that distinguishes this from every other Swiss work-adjacent route in this dataset.
